newsitem.title: POLAND: Former Polish ombudsman to head labour ministry.
newsitem.headline: Former Polish ombudsman to head labour ministry.

text.p: Poland's president said he would appoint the country's former ombudsman Tadeusz Zielinski on Friday as the new labour minister, filling a post left vacant by Andrzej Baczkowski's death last year.

"This is a sensitive man, aware of society's expectations, because as ombudsman he repeatedly heard and responded to them," PAP news agency quoted President Aleksander Kwasniewski as telling reporters.
Kwasniewski said Zielinski's biggest task would be to continue a reform, initiated by Baczkowski, of Poland's inefficient and costly social security system.
Zielinski, a 71-year-old law professor, is linked to the opposition leftist Union of Labour (UP) party and unsuccessfully ran for president in the 1995 elections on its ticket.
He will be the second opposition-rooted labour minister taken on as an independent expert in the leftist government of ex-communists and a peasant party.
Zielinski's term as Poland's ombudsman expired last year.
Baczkowski, who died of heart attack in November at the age of 41, was a former activist in the Solidarity movement which overthrew communism in 1989 but lost elections in 1993.
